result.title: Enhancing Latent World Models with Associative Memory
result.summary: World models trained via latent dynamics offer a scalable path for embodied planning, yet existing methods suffer from representational collapse, computational overhead, and limited long-horizon capability. We introduce a memory-enhanced latent world model that augments JEPA-style prediction with a content-addressable memory bank. Our approach learns high-level representations directly from observations, operating at multiple temporal scales within a shared latent space, and conditions predictions via adaptive layer normalization. To prevent collapse and ensure effective memory usage, we design two complementary losses that encourage slot diversity and balanced temporal utilization. Experiments on PushT, Tworoom, Reacher, and OGBCube demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance with a lightweight architecture, outperforming conventional latent world models on long-horizon planning tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 JEPA 式潜动态世界模型上引入内容可寻址记忆库，并设计槽位多样性与时间利用均衡两项损失来防止表示坍缩，在多个具身规划基准上验证了长程规划表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「防表示坍缩损失 + 记忆读写 + 多时间尺度共享潜空间」可能为 LVR 中的信息坍缩、证据筛选与 latent 状态更新提供方法线索，可供核查；但研究场景是具身规划而非 VLM 推理，需人工判断可否迁移。
